draft_key_information_units.information: AS Tallinna Vesi reported strong financial performance in 2025 with revenue increasing 11.4% to €72.48 million, operating profit rising 11.8% to €21.22 million, and net profit growing 7.2% to €14.24 million. The company invested €55.74 million in fixed assets.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Main financial indicators table; Statement of comprehensive income

draft_key_information_units.information: Customer revenue mix shifted significantly due to regulatory tariff harmonization: private customer sales increased 18.3% to €31.84 million from higher consumption, while business customer sales decreased 2.7% to €16.76 million following reduced tariff rates for businesses.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Sales section breakdown tables and text

draft_key_information_units.information: Cost optimization and energy transition efforts reduced electricity expenses through the new combined heat and power plant at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, which supplied 43.8% of site electricity needs and increased renewable energy consumption to 87% of total energy use (from 23% in 2020).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Energy use and energy consumption overview section

draft_key_information_units.information: Infrastructure modernization advanced with smart water meter rollout covering over 80% of customers (targeting 100% by end-2026), construction of 45.1 km of pipes (49% via trenchless methods), and launch of trenchless sewer rehabilitation service by subsidiary Watercom renewing approximately 6 km of pipes.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Investing for the Future; Watercom activities

draft_key_information_units.information: The company achieved 99.5% compliance with drinking water quality standards and was awarded 'Green Company of the Year'. Environmental initiatives included constructing 7.1 km of separate stormwater systems to reduce flooding and setting ambitious climate targets to reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% from 2020 levels by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Highlights from 2025; Sustainability Statement; Climate change section

draft_key_information_units.information: The group maintained a strong liquidity position with €11.29 million cash balance at year-end and €160 million outstanding loans carrying an average interest rate of 3.24%. A €25 million loan was drawn from the Nordic Investment Bank in December 2025 to support future investments.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of financial position; Investors section

draft_key_information_units.information: Tallinna Vesi continued its dividend policy of distributing 50-80% of annual profit, paying €0.53 per share (80% of 2024 net profit) to shareholders in June 2025, balancing returns with investment needs.

Key 2026 strategic priorities include completing the smart meter rollout, harmonizing water tariffs for residential and commercial customers by summer 2026, advancing the ozonation project at Ülemiste water treatment plant, reconstructing secondary clarifiers at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, and executing planned investments of up to €60 million.

evaluation.selection_rationale: These units were selected based on the required prioritization criteria: D1 captures headline financial performance (revenue, profit, investments). D2 addresses major period-over-period changes in customer revenue mix driven by regulatory tariff harmonization. D3 identifies key performance drivers (energy efficiency and renewable transition) that improved margins. D4 covers important segment developments in infrastructure modernization affecting service quality and customer experience. D5 includes material sustainability achievements and environmental leadership recognizing the company's strategic positioning. D6 and D7 address liquidity/financing position and shareholder returns, essential for investment analysis. D8 outlines materially important strategic developments for 2026 that guide future performance. Excluded routine boilerplate such as corporate governance details, remuneration reports, generic risk listings, accounting policy descriptions, and auditor information per evaluation guidelines. Each unit represents an independently omittable material theme supported exclusively by source document evidence without invented causal relationships.
